subject: Follow-up: FinPay evaluation — cost/TCO tests & next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: FinPay follow-up & cost/TCO next steps

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align the pilot:

Recap from discovery:
- Primary use case: customer support assistant (short to medium responses, avg. 80–120 output tokens).
- Key decision criteria: 95p latency target <150ms, predictable unit economics (per-1M tokens), SOC2 + evidence for audit, and SSO/KMS for production.
- Current baseline: FinPay is testing OpenAI + internal Bedrock endpoints; sensitivity to per-1M token costs and to tail latency.

Proposed evaluation plan (high level):
1) Cost/TCO test (3 days): measure per-1M token compute cost across realistic traffic patterns. We'll run the same prompt set against (a) Redwood hosted + caching and batching, (b) OpenAI (current baseline), and (c) Bedrock (their current test). We’ll capture raw tokens, served tokens, and effective cost after cache hits.
2) Latency test: 95th/99th percentile under production-like QPS (we recommend a small ramp to 30 QPS).
3) Quality eval: side-by-side outputs for ~200 representative prompts and your evaluation rubric.

Quick ballpark unit economics (to set expectations):
- Redwood (hosted, optimized batching + prefix cache): $45 per 1M tokens (on-demand). With batching and a 50% prefix cache hit, effective cost falls to ~$23 per 1M tokens.
- Redwood (committed/dedicated tier): $35 per 1M tokens (committed), effective ~$18 at 60% cache hit. Dedicated monthly commit options available if you want predictable throughput.
- OpenAI (public pricing baseline): ~$120 per 1M tokens (depends on model family & features).
- Bedrock (hyperscaler endpoint): ~$110–140 per 1M tokens depending on model and provisioned capacity.

Notes on cost drivers and what we'll measure:
- Batching: higher batching increases throughput efficiency but can add tail latency; we’ll capture batching windows and P95 latency tradeoffs.
- Prefix/KV cache hit rate: for assistants with repeated system prompt/context, cache can save a large fraction of tokens; we’ll instrument hit rate at request level.
- Model variant: we’ll propose a compact model for cost testing and the full model for quality checks.

Next steps I suggest:
- You share the representative prompt set and expected QPS window.
- We provision a short pilot (3 business days) and provide a temporary sandbox API key + a TCO workbook.
- We propose a kickoff call to lock test parameters — are you available Monday 3/22 or Tuesday 3/23?

I’ve attached a short TCO workbook and a security overview for SOC2 items. If procurement will be involved, please loop them in (happy to provide a procurement template).

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

Attachments: FinPay_TCO_workbook.xlsx (workbook stub), RFI_Security_Overview.pdf (summary)

From: Elena Morris <elena@finpay.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-16T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinPay follow-up & cost/TCO next steps

Thanks Aditya — very helpful summary. A few quick clarifying questions before we kick off the pilot:

1) Can you send a formal quote that includes both hosted on-demand pricing and a committed/dedicated pricing line with monthly commit options? Our procurement will want committed tier numbers for budgeting.
2) For the TCO workbook: can you include a simple sensitivity table that shows effective per-1M token cost at cache hit rates of 0%, 30%, 60%, and 80%?
3) For the latency test, can you confirm what batching windows/parameters you plan to use so we can understand P95 tradeoffs?

We’re open to a 3-day pilot as long as we have a sandbox key + clear success metrics. Procurement (I’ll loop them in once we have the committed pricing).

Also — will Redwood be able to run the pilot on a dedicated pool if we want to mimic production traffic? That’s important for apples-to-apples latency comparisons.

I’ll include Jared (procurement) when we share the formal quote. Available Monday 3/22 for a kickoff.

Best,
Elena Morris
Head of Product 
FinPay
elena@finpay.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-16T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: FinPay follow-up & cost/TCO next steps (internal)

Internal draft notes for quote and pilot design — tagging for visibility:

Pricing suggestions (internal):
- Hosted (on-demand): list $45 per 1M tokens (matches Aditya's note).
- Committed (monthly): $35 per 1M tokens at $20k/month commit; $30 per 1M tokens at $50k/month commit.
- Dedicated pool (for latency fidelity): flat monthly footprint + per-1M token billing on committed tiers; suggest offering a 30-day dedicated pilot at $8k to provision a small pool that mimics their production QPS.

Pilot/test instrumentation (metrics to capture):
- Raw tokens sent, response tokens generated, cache hits (prefix & KV), effective tokens billed, per-request latency (P50/P95/P99), batching window size, QPS, and model variant used.
- Recommend test matrix: 3 days x 3 profiles (low, med, burst) to capture variance. Include a run with 0% cache to show worst-case.

Aditya — I'll draft the formal quote + sensitivity table. Marissa — can you attach the dedicated-pool pilot template and an example TCO workbook that highlights hit-rate sensitivity?

-Marcus
Director, Solutions 
marcus.lin@redwood.com

- Instrumentation: tokens (input/output), cache hit rate (prefix & KV), batching window stats, P50/P95/P99 latency, and model used.
- Environments: Redwood hosted (with prefix cache + batching), Redwood dedicated (optional 30-day pilot), OpenAI baseline, Bedrock baseline.

- Committed: $35 per 1M tokens @ $20k/month commit (effective ~$18 per 1M at 60% cache).
- Dedicated 30-day pilot (to mimic production latency): $8k (one-time).
